<description>
`feature_torcontrol.py` can fail if the node reconnects before the test thread starts checking the backoff. This caused an intermittent CI failure on NetBSD even though the node observed the expected delay.

Record when the mock Tor server accepts the new connection and compare that timestamp with the time just before triggering the disconnect. This preserves both checks: at least half a second must have elapsed, and the node must send `PROTOCOLINFO 1` on reconnect.

On Linux, the 1.5-second delay from the issue reproduced the original failure. The updated test passed both with and without that delay.

Fixes #36934.
</description>

diff --git a/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py b/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py
index 641ab87bfd..d0ca14e0a7 100755
--- a/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py
+++ b/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py
@@ -6,9 +6,11 @@
 from contextlib import contextmanager
 import socket
 import threading
+from time import monotonic
 from test_framework.test_framework import BitcoinTestFramework
 from test_framework.util import (
     assert_equal,
+    assert_greater_than_or_equal,
     ensure_for,
     p2p_port,
 )
@@ -22,6 +24,7 @@ class MockTorControlServer:
         self.port = port
         self.sock = None
         self.conn = None
+        self.last_accept_time = None
         self.running = False
         self.thread = None
         self.received_commands = []
@@ -54,6 +57,7 @@ class MockTorControlServer:
         while self.running:
             try:
                 self.conn, _ = self.sock.accept()
+                self.last_accept_time = monotonic()
                 self.conn.settimeout(1.0)
                 self.conn_ready.set()
                 self._handle_connection(self.conn)
@@ -146,15 +150,15 @@ class TorControlTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
     @contextmanager
     def expect_disconnect(self, expect, mock_tor):
         initial_len = len(mock_tor.received_commands)
+        start = monotonic()
         yield
 
         if expect:
-            # No reconnect before the initial reconnect timeout of 1s has passed
-            ensure_for(duration=0.5, f=lambda: len(mock_tor.received_commands) == initial_len)
-            # Expect to receive a PROTOCOLINFO 1 on reconnect, bumping the received
-            # commands length.
+            # The reconnect may already have happened while the test was sending data.
             self.wait_until(lambda: len(mock_tor.received_commands) == initial_len + 1)
             assert_equal(mock_tor.received_commands[initial_len], "PROTOCOLINFO 1")
+            # Allow a half-second margin on the initial one-second backoff.
+            assert_greater_than_or_equal(mock_tor.last_accept_time - start, 0.5)
         else:
             # No disconnect, so no reconnect message
             ensure_for(duration=2, f=lambda: len(mock_tor.received_commands) == initial_len)

</patch>
